definitions.type: family of finite-dimensional real metric vector spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For m∈ℕ, V_m=EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), with norm (sum over i∈Fin m of |x_i|²)^(1/2). This is Euclidean ℝ^m. V_0 is the singleton empty-coordinate vector space. Each V_m and ℝ carry their Borel measurable structures. A product of two metric spaces in this proof has distance max of the factor distances.
I=[0,1]={t∈ℝ:0≤t≤1}; the metric is the usual real distance.

definitions.type: Hausdorff-measure family indexed by real exponent on metric spaces with Borel structure
definitions.definition: For a real exponent a and a subset T of a metric space X with Borel measurable structure, μH[a](T)=sup over r∈ℝ≥0∞, r>0, of inf over U:ℕ→Set X with T⊆⋃i U_i and ediam(U_i)≤r of ∑'i sup_{h:U_i.Nonempty}(ediam U_i)^a. Here ediam is the supremum of distances of pairs in the set, valued in ℝ≥0∞, and ediam ∅=0. The inner supremum is zero for an empty set. For a>0 this is exactly the unnormalized diameter-power countable-cover measure: empty members cost zero and no multiplicative normalization constant occurs. μH[a] denotes MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a.

binders.type: metric space with its Borel measurable structure

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of subsets of metric spaces, valued in ℝ≥0∞
definitions.definition: For a subset T of a metric space X, dimH T=sup{a∈ℝ≥0 : μH[a](T)=∞}, using the canonical embedding ℝ≥0→ℝ≥0∞ and the Borel measurable structure. This is the library Hausdorff dimension; dimH∅=0. In particular all dimension comparisons and additions in this graph take place in ℝ≥0∞ unless an explicit real conversion is written.
F=E×I={p∈V_n×ℝ:p.1∈E and p.2∈I}, with the max product metric from D001.

D=(dimH E).toReal. The operation toReal sends a finite extended nonnegative real to its real value and sends ∞ to 0, so this definition is total. ENNReal.ofReal u embeds max(u,0) into ℝ≥0∞. This definition asserts no dimension bound, finiteness or inverse identity.

inputs.statement: For the given n∈ℕ and E⊆V_n=Euclidean ℝ^n, 0≤dimH E≤n<∞. Also dimH([0,1]⊆ℝ)=1. Thus D=(dimH E).toReal is a nonnegative real with D≤n and ENNReal.ofReal D=dimH E.

For any metric space X with Borel measurable structure, A⊆X and a∈ℝ≥0: if dimH A<a then μH[a](A)=0; if a<dimH A then μH[a](A)=∞; if μH[a](A)=0 then dimH A≤a; and if μH[a](A)=∞ then a≤dimH A. All comparisons use the canonical embedding of ℝ≥0 in ℝ≥0∞.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary real s; its inequalities 0<s<D are the temporary assumption L2.

argument.text: To prove the conditional the assigned output, temporarily assume L1: 0<dimH E. N001 gives dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D and D≥0. Order preservation of the nonnegative embedding therefore gives D>0.
Fix an arbitrary real s and temporarily assume L2: 0<s<D. By N001, dimH E=ENNReal.ofReal D, so s is positive and ENNReal.ofReal s<dimH E.
Use the second implication of M002 on E⊆V_n with the nonnegative exponent s. The strict comparison from F002 yields μH[s](E)=∞.
Apply E004 at the given n,E and positive real s. It gives μH[s](E)≤μH[s+1](F). The left side is ∞ by F003; since ∞ is the greatest extended nonnegative real, this forces μH[s+1](F)=∞.
Apply the fourth implication of M002 to F in the max product metric at nonnegative exponent s+1. From F004 we obtain ENNReal.ofReal(s+1)≤dimH F.
Discharge L2 and universally quantify s. Under L1 we have F006: for every real b with 0<b<D, ENNReal.ofReal(b+1)≤dimH F.

produces.statement: For every real b, if 0<b<D then ENNReal.ofReal(b+1)≤dimH F.

argument.text: Still under L1, suppose for contradiction L3: dimH F<dimH E+1. By N001, dimH E+1=ENNReal.ofReal(D+1)<∞, because D≥0 is finite. Hence dimH F<∞.
Define T=(dimH F).toReal. F007 implies T≥0, ENNReal.ofReal T=dimH F, and T<D+1 by order comparison of finite nonnegative embeddings; D+1>0 by F001.

produces.statement: T≥0, ENNReal.ofReal T=dimH F, and T<D+1.

argument.text: Define v=max(0,T-1) and s0=(v+D)/2. Since D>0 by F001 and T-1<D by F008, we have 0≤v<D. Thus 0<s0<D and T-1≤v<s0. Applying F006 at s0 gives ENNReal.ofReal(s0+1)≤dimH F=ENNReal.ofReal T. Both arguments of ofReal are nonnegative, so s0+1≤T. But T-1<s0 implies T<s0+1, a contradiction. Discharge L3; the linear order now gives dimH E+1≤dimH F under L1.
Discharge L1 by implication introduction. We have proved: if 0<dimH E then dimH E+1≤dimH F. This is the assigned output, and the positive-dimension condition remains precisely its antecedent.
